summary: Gates Cambridge Scholarships are full-cost awards for non-UK citizens doing a full-time postgraduate degree (PhD, MLitt or most one-year master's) at the University of Cambridge. They cover the full cost of study plus maintenance. Winners are academically outstanding people with a clear reason for their course, a record of leadership and a real commitment to improving the lives of others.
lookfor: Outstanding intellectual ability and academic achievement — departments only nominate their top applicants
A strong, specific reason for choosing this Cambridge course and how it fits your future plans
Commitment to improving the lives of others — past, present and future
Capacity for leadership, shown in any setting
PhD: a feasible research proposal developed with a potential supervisor
cycle: For 2027 entry, international (non-US) applicants must submit the Cambridge application with the Gates section by 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, depending on the course's funding deadline (check your course page). Departments rank applicants December–February; shortlisted candidates are told by 8 March 2027; interviews are 22–23 March 2027; offers go out in early April 2027 and must be accepted within 72 hours.

eligibility.q: Are you a citizen of a country other than the United Kingdom?
eligibility.no: Gates Cambridge is not open to UK citizens. Look at Cambridge Trust or research council funding.

eligibility.q: Are you applying for a full-time PhD, MLitt or eligible one-year postgraduate course at Cambridge?
eligibility.no: MBA, EMBA, MFin, PGCE, MASt, undergraduate and most part-time courses are not funded. Choose an eligible course or look at other Cambridge funding.

eligibility.q: Is your academic record among the very best in your cohort (usually a First Class or top 2:1 equivalent)?
eligibility.no: Departments nominate only the most academically outstanding applicants. Consider Chevening or Commonwealth awards, which weigh leadership or development more.

eligibility.q: If applying for a PhD, have you not already started the PhD you want funded?
eligibility.no: Gates does not fund the remainder of a PhD already under way.

eligibility.q: Can you show leadership and a commitment to improving others' lives with concrete examples?
eligibility.no: Build evidence first (community projects, mentoring, initiatives) and apply in a later year.

steps.title: Check eligibility and your course's funding deadline
steps.why: There is no separate Gates application — you apply through the Cambridge course application before that course's funding deadline.
do: Open the Gates Cambridge eligibility page and confirm your course is eligible.
Open the Cambridge Course Directory and find your course.
On the course page, note the funding deadline: 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027.
Note the course's entry requirements and English test requirement.
tips: Use the funding deadline, not the later admission deadline.
avoid: Applying after the funding deadline — you will not be considered for Gates.
check: My course is eligible and I know its funding deadline.

steps.title: Study the four selection criteria
steps.why: Your statement, references and interview are all judged against the same four criteria.
do: Open the criteria page and copy the four criteria into a document.
Under each, list your three strongest pieces of evidence.
Read the 'how we select' page to understand departmental nomination and interviews.
tips: 'Improving the lives of others' is read broadly — you define it, but you must show it with action.
avoid: Relying on grades alone; all four criteria must be very strong.
check: I have evidence for all four criteria.

steps.title: PhD and research MPhil: contact a potential supervisor
steps.why: Supervisor fit drives departmental ranking, and Gates expects research applicants to have developed a project with a supervisor.
do: Find two or three Cambridge academics working on your topic via department pages.
Read their recent papers.
Email a short introduction, a one-page project outline and your CV, asking if they would supervise.
Refine your proposal with their feedback.
tips: Name the supervisor in your application if the portal asks.
avoid: Proposing a topic no one at Cambridge can supervise.
check: I have had a reply from at least one potential supervisor.

steps.title: Open the Applicant Portal and plan the fee
steps.why: You must pay the application fee before you can submit, and Nigeria is not on the automatic fee-waiver list.
do: From your course page, open the Applicant Portal and register.
Start the application and look at every section, including the funding section with the Gates Cambridge questions.
Check the fee (£85 for most postgraduate courses; £20 for doctoral courses as of September 2025 — confirm on the fee page).
Check if your country is on the waiver list; if not, arrange a Visa or Mastercard that works for foreign payments (some naira cards have low international limits).
tips: Waiver requests (where eligible) are due 24 November 2026 for the December deadline, and 11 December 2026 for January.
avoid: Finding on deadline day that your card is declined.
check: My account is open and I can pay the fee.

steps.title: Gather transcripts, CV and English evidence
steps.why: Cambridge needs transcripts for every degree and English evidence if English is not your first language.
do: Request transcripts for each degree from your university's registry or transcript portal (budget the naira fee and time).
Update a two-page academic CV: education, research, publications, awards, leadership, service.
Check the English requirement on your course page and book IELTS/TOEFL early if needed.
Prepare any written work sample your course asks for.
tips: Upload a scanned transcript now; official copies may be requested later if you get an offer.
avoid: Missing the English test — a late score can block an offer.
check: All supporting documents are scanned and ready.

steps.title: Gates question 1: academic excellence
steps.why: Shows the intellectual ability criterion in your own words.
do: Pick two or three achievements: class rank, prizes, research, publications.
Explain what each shows about how you think, not just the grade.
Keep it tight — about 200 words.
tips: Context helps: 'top of 120 students' is clearer than 'First Class'.
avoid: Repeating your CV line by line.

steps.prompt: Describe how, through your education and past experiences, you have displayed academic excellence.

steps.title: Gates question 2: why this course at Cambridge
steps.why: Shows the 'reasons for choice of course' criterion.
do: Name the course and what specifically at Cambridge you need (supervisor, lab, modules, collections).
Link it to the next step of your career.
Show you have the skills to complete it.
tips: Name people, groups or resources — be specific to Cambridge.
steps.prompt: Explain why you want to study this specific course at Cambridge, and how it will facilitate your future plans.

steps.title: Gates question 3: improving the lives of others
steps.why: This is the defining Gates criterion.
do: Choose one or two examples where your action improved others' lives.
Describe the need, what you did, and the result with numbers.
Connect it to how your Cambridge degree lets you do more.
tips: Show a pattern over time, not a single event.
avoid: Abstract statements like 'I am passionate about helping people'.
check: It is under 2,100 characters and has a measurable result.
steps.prompt: Provide an example, or examples, of how you have demonstrated a commitment to improving the lives of others.

steps.title: Gates question 4: leadership
do: Choose one strong example where you led people to a result.
Explain the challenge, how you led, and what changed.
Reflect briefly on what you learned and how you will lead in future.
tips: Leadership can be academic, community or professional.
avoid: Using the same example as question 3.
steps.prompt: Provide an example, or examples, of how you have demonstrated a capacity for leadership.

steps.title: PhD: write the research proposal (and course personal statement)
steps.why: PhD applicants must submit a research proposal; it drives departmental ranking.
do: Check the word/character limit on your course page or in the portal.
Cover: research questions and objectives, how it relates to existing work, significance, your background, methods and plan, scope and timeline.
Add ethics or risk notes if relevant.
Ask your potential supervisor for comments.
Write the course personal statement separately if your course requires it.
tips: Fit with Cambridge supervisors and resources is essential.
avoid: Exceeding the limit or ignoring what counts in it (e.g. footnotes).
check: Proposal fits the limit and has a clear question and method.
steps.prompt: Research proposal: questions, context, significance, methods and plan.
steps.limit: Set by your course — check the course page or Applicant Portal.

steps.title: Line up three referees
steps.why: Gates applicants need three references: two academic for admission plus one Gates reference on the scholarship criteria. All must arrive by the deadline.
do: Ask two academics who know your work well for the admission references.
Ask one person who can speak to your leadership and commitment to others (employer, NGO leader, or an academic) for the Gates reference.
Send each your CV, Gates answers and course choice.
Enter their emails in the portal early so the Referee Portal sends them links.
Remind them two weeks and three days before the deadline.
tips: The Gates reference rates you as exceptional, strong, not strong or weak — pick someone who will say exceptional with examples.
Referees need to submit a separate reference for each course you apply to.
check: All three references show as received in the portal.

steps.title: Complete the funding section, pay and submit
steps.why: Ticking Gates Cambridge in the funding section and answering its questions is your Gates application.
do: Fill all admission sections and choose a College (or let the University choose).
In the funding section, select Gates Cambridge and paste your four answers.
PhD: upload the research proposal.
Upload CV, transcripts and English evidence.
Pay the fee and submit; save the confirmation.
tips: Submit a few days before the funding deadline so you can fix payment problems.
avoid: Forgetting to select Gates in the funding section.

links.t: Watch: Study in the UK for free|| Gates Cambridge scholarship 2027 || (Emmanuella Osarodion)

steps.title: Prepare for the Gates interview if shortlisted
steps.why: Shortlisted candidates (told by 8 March 2027) have a 25–30 minute panel interview on 22–23 March 2027, in person or online.
do: Re-read your application and research the Gates Cambridge Scholar community.
Prepare answers on why Gates, why this course, your academic plans and career path.
Expect questions from academics in your broad area (Arts, Biological, Physical or Social Sciences).
Do two mock interviews, one with a specialist in your field.
Prepare one or two thoughtful questions for the end.
tips: Know how you will contribute to the Gates community, not just benefit from it.
avoid: Over-technical answers the whole panel cannot follow.
check: I can explain my research and its value to a non-specialist in two minutes.

links.t: Watch: Applying for Gates Cambridge: What does the interview process involve? (GatesCambridge)

steps.title: Accept, meet offer conditions and get your visa
steps.why: Offers come in early April 2027 and must be accepted within 72 hours. You also need to meet Cambridge's academic conditions.
do: Accept the Gates offer within 72 hours.
Meet Cambridge offer conditions (final transcript, English score).
Apply for your UK student visa once you receive your CAS.
If unsuccessful, other Cambridge funding may still be available — check the funding search.
tips: Unsuccessful applicants do not get feedback, so review your weakest criterion yourself.
check: I have accepted and know my conditions.

faq.q: Is there a separate Gates application?
faq.a: No. You answer the Gates questions in the funding section of the Cambridge course application.

faq.q: Does applying for Gates hurt my admission chances?
faq.a: Gates selection is needs-blind; your admission is decided by the department.

faq.q: Can my Gates referee also be an academic referee?
faq.a: It can be someone who also writes an academic reference if they can speak to the Gates criteria.

faq.q: Is Nigeria eligible for the application fee waiver?
faq.a: Nigeria is not on the current automatic waiver list. Check the waiver page for your country.

faq.q: Will I get feedback if I am not selected?
faq.a: No, Gates Cambridge does not give feedback to unsuccessful applicants.
